symptom: Kick drum on every quarter note without variation. The most common rhythmic pattern in electronic music — using it without creative intent signals a lack of rhythmic imagination.
repair: If you need a steady pulse, make it irregular — skip beats, add extra hits, or use a non-kick sound for the pulse. The pulse should feel like a creative choice, not a default.

symptom: The 'tss tss tss tss' on every off-beat. Instantly signals 'generic dance music' regardless of context.
repair: Replace hi-hat with any other high-frequency element used rhythmically: gated noise, filtered metallic resonance, processed sample, or simply an irregular pattern on a non-standard sound.

symptom: The backbeat snare — the backbone of rock, pop, and most EDM. Using it locks the music into a familiar structural grid.
repair: Move the backbeat accent to an unexpected position, remove it entirely, or replace it with a non-snare sound (metallic hit, noise burst, pitched tone).

cliche: All structural changes on cycle boundaries 4, 8, 16, 32
symptom: Every addition, removal, or change happens exactly on powers-of-two cycle boundaries. This grid-locked structure is immediately predictable.
repair: Make at least 2 changes on non-power-of-two cycles (3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17). Make at least one change mid-cycle.

symptom: Applying rand() or sometimesBy() to many parameters without a clear musical goal. Random ≠ creative — it becomes uniform, characterless noise.
repair: Replace random modulation with intentional, patterned modulation. Use sequenced automations ('<a b c>'), slow LFOs, and specific probability events that serve a clear textural or rhythmic purpose.

cliche: Chord progression as the primary structural device
symptom: Using chord changes (I-IV-V-I etc.) to create musical movement. This is the default Western music structure — it immediately makes the piece sound conventional.
repair: Remove all chord progressions. Movement should come from texture, space, rhythm, and timbre. If harmonic movement is needed, shift one note by a semitone over a very long time.

symptom: The EDM build-up (filter sweep + snare roll) leading to a drop (all elements return at full intensity). Instantly dates and genres the music.
repair: If you need a structural climax, use textural density, spatial expansion, or rhythmic complexity to create peak moments — not the build/drop formula.

cliche: Static timbre — no sound evolution over time
symptom: Every sound sounds the same at the beginning and end of the piece. No filter movement, no textural change, no timbral evolution.
repair: Ensure at least 2 elements have significant timbral evolution over the course of the piece. Filter sweeps, distortion changes, reverb changes — the sounds should age.

cliche: Default preset sounds with no processing
symptom: Using synth presets, drum machine defaults, or recognizable sample-library sounds without significant processing or transformation.
repair: Process every preset beyond recognition. Filter heavily, layer with noise, apply effects creatively. The source should not be identifiable.

cliche: Steady-state mix — no dynamics, no spatial movement
symptom: All elements stay at the same volume, same pan position, same spatial depth for the entire piece. The mix is a static photograph, not a living environment.
repair: Give at least 3 elements spatial movement over time. Gain modulation, pan drift, reverb changes — the mix should breathe.
